methodology: Survey-weighted exploratory analysis using CDC final post-stratification expansion weights (_LLCPWT)

screening_adherence.interpretation: Among US adults meeting USPSTF 2021 LDCT screening criteria, fewer than 10% received annual screening, demonstrating a massive screening under-utilization gap.

logistic_regression_copd.model: COPD (Yes/No) ~ Pack-Years (per 10y) + Age Group + Female Sex

research_hypotheses.hypothesis_statement: Cumulative tobacco smoke exposure measured in pack-years exhibits a monotonic, supra-linear association with self-reported COPD diagnosis, even after adjusting for chronological age and sex.
research_hypotheses.rationale: Empirical odds ratio of 1.25 per 10 pack-years indicates heavy cumulative airway remodeling; patients with 30+ pack-years have >2.0x higher comorbidity prevalence.
research_hypotheses.testable_prediction: Independent Bangladesh clinical cohorts will demonstrate comparable dose-response gradients, though potentially left-shifted due to higher tar/nicotine content in bidi products.
research_hypotheses.confounding_factors: Occupational particulate exposure, biomass cooking smoke, secondhand smoke, age.

research_hypotheses.hypothesis_statement: Fewer than 15% of asymptomatic individuals meeting clinical criteria for lung cancer screening receive recommended annual LDCT scans, with non-adherence heavily concentrated among rural, lower-income, and uninsured demographics.
research_hypotheses.rationale: BRFSS 2022 shows 9.35% population-weighted adherence among USPSTF eligible cohort, revealing a profound implementation gap.
research_hypotheses.testable_prediction: In Bangladesh, screening adherence among high-risk individuals will be even lower (<2%) due to limited CT scanner availability and out-of-pocket costs.
research_hypotheses.confounding_factors: Healthcare access, provider recommendation bias, geographic distance to tertiary imaging centers.

research_hypotheses.hypothesis_statement: Former smokers who have quit for >10 years continue to experience elevated rates of chronic respiratory symptoms (cough, phlegm, dyspnea) relative to never-smokers.
research_hypotheses.rationale: Airway inflammation and permanent parenchymal damage persist post-cessation, creating false clinical reassurance if former smokers are dismissed without symptom triage.
research_hypotheses.testable_prediction: Validates Lungent's Phase 1 clinical invariant that former smoking status does NOT suppress acute symptom triage.
research_hypotheses.confounding_factors: Duration of former smoking, baseline pack-years prior to cessation, occupational exposures.

research_hypotheses.hypothesis_statement: In populations with non-commercial biomass cooking fuel exposures, non-smoking females will exhibit chronic respiratory symptom and airway obstruction rates comparable to moderate tobacco smokers.
research_hypotheses.rationale: BRFSS cannot test this directly due to US electric/gas cooking dominance, highlighting a vital external validity gap requiring Bangladesh-specific data collection.
research_hypotheses.testable_prediction: Cross-sectional comparison between rural Bangladesh wood/dung fuel users and urban LPG users will reveal significant odds ratio elevation for respiratory symptoms independent of tobacco.
research_hypotheses.confounding_factors: Household ventilation, kitchen location, hours spent cooking per day.
